column3: The Hebrew names “the ears of the LORD” and repeats the LORD’s name as the hearer; BSB uses “the hearing of the LORD” and then “He.”
The Hebrew repeats Moses’ name as the one praying; BSB uses “he.”
The Hebrew uses active singular “he called the name of that place”; BSB uses passive “that place was called.”
The Hebrew repeats the craving root, without explicitly naming “other food”; BSB supplies that object for the craving.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “our soul is dry” and “our eyes” are toward the manna; BSB says “our appetite is gone” and “there is nothing to see.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew joins cooking and making cakes with “and”; BSB uses “or” between boiling and shaping into cakes.
The Hebrew says the manna fell “on” the dew; BSB says “with it.”
The Hebrew says each person was “at the entrance of his tent” and that it was evil “in the eyes of Moses”; BSB uses plural entrances and tents and says Moses “was also displeased.”
The Hebrew says “in Your eyes”; BSB uses “in Your sight.”
The Hebrew uses a singular collective pronoun for the people when bearing them and giving them birth, and names a nursing infant; BSB uses plural “them” and the broader “an infant.”
The Hebrew ends the demand with “and let us eat”; BSB expresses this as “to eat.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew emphasizes killing by repeating the verb; BSB adds “right now” to the request.
The Hebrew repeats “elders” for those known to Moses; BSB varies the second occurrence as “leaders.”
The Hebrew says they will “bear with you” the burden; BSB expresses this as helping Moses bear it.
The Hebrew says it was “good for us in Egypt”; BSB makes this comparative, “better off in Egypt.”
The Hebrew repeats “not” and the day word for each duration; BSB compresses the list with “or.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew does not explicitly say “all our” before the flocks and herds; BSB adds those words. For the fish the Hebrew says “gathered”; BSB says “caught.”
The Hebrew uses “the hand of the LORD” and asks whether His word will “meet you”; BSB says “the LORD’s arm” and “come to pass.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew refers to the Spirit on “him”; BSB supplies Moses’ name.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “the young man” and includes a separate “and he said”; BSB says “A young man” and incorporates the speech into the reporting clause.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses the wishing expression “Who will give”; BSB makes the wish explicit as “I wish.”
The Hebrew says Moses “was gathered” to the camp; BSB says he “returned.”
